title: Weird Physics · Falling through the Earth

post.title: Jump into a tunnel through Earth: 42 minutes to the other side 🕳️🌍
post.description:
In the classic physics thought experiment (a straight tunnel, no air, no heat, a uniform non-rotating Earth), you'd fall through the planet in about 42 minutes, hitting about 28,000 km/h at the centre. The weird part: any straight tunnel between two points on the surface takes the same 42 minutes, even a short one between neighbouring cities. And it's exactly half the 84-minute orbit of a satellite skimming the surface.

Computed from NASA's Earth Fact Sheet (radius 6,371 km, GM 398,600 km³/s²): https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html

Image: NASA / JSC (Apollo 17 'Blue Marble'). Narration uses a synthetic voice.

narration: Dig a tunnel straight through the Earth, and jump in.
You'd pop out the other side in about 42 minutes.

params.label: to fall all the way through the Earth

narration: Forget air, heat and rock for a moment.
Gravity pulls you down, faster and faster.
At the centre you're doing about 28,000 kilometres an hour.
Then gravity slows you down, and you stop right at the far end.
Tilt the tunnel, so it's a short cut between two nearby cities.
A shorter tunnel is less steep, so you fall more gently, and the two effects cancel exactly.
And 42 minutes is exactly half of one orbit, for a satellite skimming the surface.
Falling through the planet and flying around it take the same time.

params.label: one orbit skimming the surface: half of it is 42 min
